items.followUp: Explain why atomic radius generally increases down a group.

rubric.why: Identifies increasing nuclear charge while added electrons enter the same main shell.
rubric.description: Across a period, proton number increases and electrons are added to the same main shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same shell.

rubric.why: Connects the greater nuclear attraction to the decrease in atomic size.
rubric.description: The stronger nuclear attraction pulls electrons closer to the nucleus, decreasing atomic size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking stronger nuclear attraction with decreasing atomic size.

modelAnswer: Across a period, the number of protons increases while the added electrons enter the same main shell.
The stronger nuclear attraction pulls the electrons closer to the nucleus, so atomic size decreases.

items.followUp: What is shielding effect, and which electrons shield the valence electrons?

rubric.why: Defines effective nuclear charge as the positive charge experienced by an electron.
rubric.description: Effective nuclear charge is the net positive charge experienced by an electron in an atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the positive charge experienced by an electron.

rubric.why: Recognizes that shielding by other electrons reduces the nuclear attraction experienced by an electron.
rubric.description: It is the nuclear attraction remaining after shielding by other electrons is taken into account.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shielding by other electrons affects the remaining nuclear attraction.

modelAnswer: Effective nuclear charge is the net positive charge experienced by an electron in an atom.
It is the nuclear attraction remaining after shielding by other electrons is taken into account.

items.followUp: Why are noble gases generally unreactive?

rubric.why: Identifies the complete outermost shell as the key feature of noble-gas configurations.
rubric.description: Noble gases have a complete outermost electron shell, an octet for most noble gases and a duplet for helium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the outermost shell is complete, or identifying the octet or duplet.

rubric.why: Explains that the configuration is stable and is the arrangement other atoms tend to attain.
rubric.description: The complete shell gives noble gases a stable configuration; other atoms tend to attain it by gaining, losing or sharing electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the configuration to stability or explaining that other atoms tend to attain it.

modelAnswer: Noble gases have a complete outermost electron shell: an octet for most noble gases and a duplet for helium.
This gives them a stable electronic configuration; other atoms tend to gain, lose or share electrons to attain a noble gas configuration.

items.followUp: How do stronger intermolecular forces affect the energy needed to boil a liquid?

rubric.why: States that stronger intermolecular forces raise the boiling point.
rubric.description: Stronger intermolecular forces result in a higher boiling point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that stronger intermolecular forces increase the boiling point.

rubric.why: Explains the effect by referring to the energy required to overcome attractions between molecules.
rubric.description: More energy is needed to overcome the forces and separate the molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that more energy is required to overcome the forces or separate the molecules.

modelAnswer: Stronger intermolecular forces result in a higher boiling point.
More energy is needed to overcome these forces and separate the molecules.
